stem: Which formula gives the **acid test (quick) ratio**?

options.rationale: Correct: inventory is excluded as the least liquid current asset.
This is the current ratio.
Receivables stay in; only inventory is removed.
This is the ratio upside down.

explanation: Acid test = (current assets − inventory) ÷ current liabilities, written x : 1.

stem: Current assets are US\$27,300 and current liabilities US\$15,600. What is the current ratio?

options.rationale: Current liabilities have been divided by current assets.
This is working capital in dollars, not a ratio.
The ratio has been multiplied by 100 like a percentage.

stem: Current assets US\$41,600 (including inventory of US\$22,400); current liabilities US\$16,000. What is the acid test ratio?

options.rationale: This is the current ratio: inventory has not been removed.
This divides inventory alone by current liabilities.
Inventory has been added to current liabilities.

stem: Why is inventory left out of the acid test ratio?

options.rationale: Inventory is a current asset.

options.content: It may take time to sell and then to turn into cash
options.rationale: Correct: inventory is the least liquid current asset.

options.content: It is valued at selling price
options.rationale: Inventory is valued at cost (or net realisable value if lower).

options.content: It is already included in current liabilities
options.rationale: Inventory is an asset, not a liability.

explanation: The acid test asks whether debts could be paid without relying on selling inventory.

stem: A business has current assets of US\$30,000 and current liabilities of US\$20,000. It pays a supplier US\$5,000 from the bank. What is the new current ratio?

options.rationale: This is the ratio before the payment.
Only current assets have been reduced; current liabilities fall too.
Only current liabilities have been reduced; the bank balance falls too.

explanation: After the payment: 25,000 ÷ 15,000 = 1.67 : 1. Working capital is still 10,000.
hints: Both the bank (a current asset) and trade payables (a current liability) fall.

stem: Which transaction would **improve** a trader's acid test ratio?

options.rationale: This adds to current liabilities but not to liquid assets.

options.content: Receiving cash from a credit customer
options.rationale: One liquid asset replaces another; the ratio is unchanged.
Liquid assets fall with no fall in current liabilities.

options.content: Selling surplus inventory for cash at cost
options.rationale: Correct: inventory (excluded) becomes cash (included).

explanation: Turning inventory into cash raises liquid assets while current liabilities stay the same.
hints: Which items are in the top of the acid test fraction?

stem: A trader's current ratio is 4.8 : 1, much higher than similar shops. What does this most likely suggest?

options.content: The trader cannot pay her debts as they fall due
options.rationale: That would be shown by a low ratio.

options.content: The trader's profit margin is very high
options.rationale: The current ratio measures liquidity, not profitability.

options.content: Resources are tied up in idle current assets
options.rationale: Correct: very high ratios suggest resources not being used well.

options.content: The trader has too many non-current liabilities
options.rationale: Non-current liabilities are not part of the current ratio.

explanation: A very high current ratio can mean excess inventory, slow collection of debts or cash that could be earning a return.

stem: In ZIMSEC questions the acid test ratio is usually called the …

options.rationale: This is another name for the current ratio.
This is an efficiency ratio.
Correct: the ZIMSEC syllabus lists it as the quick ratio.
This is a profitability ratio.

explanation: ZIMSEC: quick ratio; Cambridge: acid test (liquid) ratio.

stem: A bank overdraft is included in current liabilities when calculating the current ratio.
explanation: True. An overdraft is repayable on demand, so it is a current liability.

stem: A business with a high profit for the year must also have a high current ratio.
explanation: False. Profit and liquidity are different. A profitable business can be short of cash, for example if its money is tied up in inventory or new equipment.

stem: A business has a current ratio above 1 : 1. Match each transaction with its effect on the current ratio.

left.content: Paying a trade payable from the bank
Receiving cash from a trade receivable
Taking a five-year bank loan into the bank account

explanation: Equal falls in both (paying a payable) raise a ratio above 1; equal rises (credit purchases) lower it; swapping one current asset for another changes nothing; a long-term loan adds cash only; paying an expense lowers current assets only.
hints: Work out what happens to the top and the bottom of the fraction.

payload.template: Current ratio = current assets ÷ {{blank:a}}. Acid test ratio = (current assets − {{blank:b}}) ÷ current liabilities.

explanation: Both ratios compare current assets with current liabilities; the acid test removes inventory.

A trader's current liabilities are US\$18,400 and her current ratio is 1.6 : 1. Calculate her current assets.
hints: Current assets = current ratio × current liabilities.

stem: Tatenda's acid test ratio has fallen from 1.1 : 1 to 0.6 : 1. Suggest **three** actions he could take to improve his liquidity.

points.description: Collect debts faster / offer cash discounts for prompt payment
Reduce inventory levels / sell surplus inventory
Introduce more capital / take a long-term loan instead of an overdraft / reduce drawings / negotiate longer credit from suppliers

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: He could offer customers a small discount to pay sooner, sell off slow-moving inventory to raise cash, and replace his overdraft with a long-term loan or put in more of his own capital.

hints: Raise liquid assets or reduce current liabilities.

stem: Explain why a supplier would look at a customer's liquidity ratios before giving credit.

points.description: The ratios show whether the customer can pay short-term debts
A low ratio warns that the supplier might not be paid on time / at all

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The supplier wants to be paid within the credit period. The ratios show whether the customer has enough current assets to cover its short-term debts; low ratios suggest a risk of late payment or bad debt.

explanation: Creditors are users who care most about short-term solvency.

|  | 2024 US\$ | 2025 US\$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Inventory | 12,600 | 19,750 |
| Trade receivables | 6,800 | 9,300 |
| Bank | 4,100 | – |
| Trade payables | 9,200 | 13,600 |
| Bank overdraft | – | 2,900 |

parts.label: (a)

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the current ratio for 2025, as x : 1 to two decimal places.

parts.stem: Calculate the acid test (quick) ratio for 2025, as x : 1 to two decimal places.

parts.stem: Comment on Thandeka's liquidity in 2025 compared with 2024.

points.description: Current ratio fell from 2.55 : 1 to 1.76 : 1 but is still above 1 : 1
Acid test fell from 1.18 : 1 to 0.56 : 1: below 1 : 1, so she depends on selling inventory to pay debts
Inventory has risen sharply (12,600 to 19,750) while the bank balance has become an overdraft
Conclusion: liquidity has worsened; she may struggle to pay suppliers on time

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Her current ratio has fallen from 2.55 : 1 to 1.76 : 1, which still looks acceptable, but the acid test has dropped from 1.18 : 1 to 0.56 : 1. Much of her money is now tied up in furniture: inventory rose by US\$7,150 while the bank balance of US\$4,100 turned into an overdraft of US\$2,900. Her liquidity has worsened and she may struggle to pay suppliers without selling stock quickly.

explanation: 2024: current 2.55 : 1, acid test 1.18 : 1. 2025: current 1.76 : 1, acid test 0.56 : 1.
hints: The overdraft is a current liability; there is no bank asset in 2025.
